name: Commerce
topics: The stock exchange and capital market
Business documents, discounts and terms of trade

questions.q: Which of the following best defines commerce?
o: The production of raw materials needed by industries
The simple buying and selling of goods only
The study of how government raises and spends revenue
The sum of all activities connected with the distribution of goods and services from the producer to the final consumer
questions.e: Commerce covers trade (buying and selling) and all the aids to trade such as transport, banking, insurance, warehousing and advertising that help move goods from producers to consumers. It is wider than just buying and selling.
questions.p: Commerce na everything wey dey help goods and service waka from the person wey produce am go reach the final buyer. E no be just buying and selling alone, e include transport, bank, insurance and the rest.

questions.q: Occupations can be grouped into commerce, industry and direct service. Which of the following is an example of a direct service occupation?
o: A trader who exports palm oil to Ghana
A banker who grants loans to cocoa farmers in Ondo State
A doctor who treats patients at a general hospital in Enugu
A warehouse keeper who stores bags of rice before sale
questions.e: Direct services are personal services rendered straight to people without passing through trade or its aids, such as medicine, teaching and legal practice. Banking, warehousing and trading are all aids to trade or commercial activities, not direct services.
questions.p: Direct service na wen person dey serve another person their self-self, like doctor wey dey treat patient. Banking, warehouse and trading na aids to trade, dem no be direct service.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa owns a company that mines tin ore on the Jos Plateau and sells the raw ore to processing firms. His business belongs to which class of industry?
questions.e: Extractive industries obtain raw materials directly from the land, sea or air, such as mining, fishing and lumbering. Since Alhaji Musa simply mines and sells raw tin ore without processing it, his business is an extractive industry.
questions.p: Extractive industry na the one wey dey collect raw material from ground, water or air, like mining. Since Alhaji Musa just dey mine tin ore and sell am raw, na extractive industry be dat.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT regarded as an aid to trade?
questions.e: Aids to trade are services that make buying and selling easier, such as transport, insurance, banking, warehousing and advertising. Farming is a production activity (primary production), not a service that assists trade.
questions.p: Aids to trade na services wey dey make trade sweet, like transport, insurance and advertising. Farming na production work, e no be aid to trade.

questions.q: A Nigerian company imports textile materials from China and, without using them, re-exports the same materials to Chad. What type of trade is this company engaged in?
questions.e: Entrepot trade occurs when a country imports goods from one country and re-exports them, in the same or slightly altered form, to another country without consuming them. The Nigerian company here is simply acting as a middleman between China and Chad.
questions.p: Entrepot trade na wen country import goods come re-export am go another country without using am. Na so dis Nigeria company take dey do am between China and Chad.

questions.q: Mrs. Ibeh harvests large quantities of yam in October, but the demand for the yam is highest during the Christmas period in December. Which activity solves the hindrance to trade created by this difference in time between production and consumption?
questions.e: The gap between the time goods are produced and the time they are needed is the hindrance of time, and it is overcome by warehousing, which stores goods safely until they are required. Transport solves distance problems, advertising solves lack of information, and banking solves finance problems, so they do not fit this situation.
questions.p: The problem na say the yam ready for October but people need am for December, na hindrance of time. Warehousing na im dey solve am because e go store the yam well well until December reach. Transport, advertising and banking no fit solve dis kind problem.

questions.q: A company in Nnewi assembles motorcycles using parts imported from abroad and sells the finished motorcycles to dealers. What type of occupation is this company engaged in?
questions.e: Manufacturing involves changing raw materials or parts into finished or more useful goods, which is exactly what the Nnewi company does by assembling imported parts into motorcycles. Extractive occupations get raw materials from nature, genetic occupations involve breeding plants/animals, and commercial occupations deal with trade and its aids, none of which matches assembling motorcycles.
questions.p: Manufacturing na wen dem take raw material or parts turn am to finish product, like dis company wey dey assemble motorcycle from imported parts. Extractive na for raw material from nature, genetic na for breeding, commercial na for trade matter, none of dem match dis one.

questions.q: In Commerce, production is best described as the process of:
o: moving goods from the farm to the market
buying goods cheaply and selling them at a higher price
creating utility by making goods and services available to satisfy human wants
storing goods safely until customers are ready to buy them
questions.e: Production is any economic activity that creates utility (value) by making goods or services available for consumption, whether through growing, making, moving, storing or selling. It is not just buying-and-selling or storage alone.
questions.p: Production na any work wey dey create value make goods and services dey available for people to use. E no be only buy-and-sell or keeping goods for store.

questions.q: Which of the following activities is an example of primary production?
o: Baking of bread inside a factory in Aba
Processing of palm fruits into palm oil in a mill
Catching of fish by fishermen along the Badagry coast
Selling of ankara fabrics at Balogun market
questions.e: Primary production involves extracting raw materials directly from nature, such as fishing, farming and mining. Baking bread and processing palm fruits are secondary (manufacturing) production, while selling fabric is tertiary (commerce/distributive trade).
questions.p: Primary production na when you dey collect raw material straight from nature, like fishing or farming. To bake bread or process palm oil na secondary production, and to sell cloth na tertiary.

questions.q: Tunde grows cassava on his farm, Ngozi processes the cassava into garri in her mill, and Chidi then transports the garri to Mile 12 market and sells it to traders. Whose activity represents secondary production?
questions.e: Secondary production involves changing raw materials into a new, more useful form, such as processing cassava into garri. Tunde's farming is primary production, while Chidi's transporting and selling is tertiary production.
questions.p: Secondary production na when you change raw material into another useful form, like to process cassava become garri. Tunde dey do primary (farming) and Chidi dey do tertiary (selling/transport).

questions.q: Among the four major factors of production, which one earns rent as its reward for being used in the production process?
questions.e: Land, which includes all natural resources, earns rent when it is used by others for farming, building or mining. Labour earns wages, capital earns interest, and the entrepreneur earns profit.
questions.p: Land, wey be all natural resources, dey earn rent when people use am for farm or building. Labour get wages, capital get interest, entrepreneur get profit.

questions.q: Which of the following best illustrates indirect production?
o: A farmer eating the yam he harvested with his own family
A fisherman selling part of his catch to a trader who resells it to consumers
A carpenter making a chair for his personal use at home
A woman cooking food only for her own household
questions.e: Indirect production occurs when goods are produced not for the producer's own use but for exchange through a market, often passing through middlemen before reaching the final consumer. The other options describe direct production, where goods are consumed by the producer without any exchange.
questions.p: Indirect production na when person produce goods not for im own use but to sell am through market, maybe pass through middleman reach the final consumer. The other options na direct production, wey mean say the producer na im dey use the goods.

questions.q: Mr. Obi's shoe factory breaks down production into many small, repetitive tasks so that each worker performs only one simple operation all day. A major disadvantage of this extreme form of division of labour is that workers may:
o: earn higher wages because output per worker increases
reduce the overall cost of producing each pair of shoes
produce shoes of better quality because of specialization
become bored and lose interest due to the monotony of repeating the same task
questions.e: While division of labour can raise output and lower unit cost, performing the same narrow task repeatedly often leads to boredom, fatigue and loss of job satisfaction, which can reduce morale and increase errors or absenteeism. The other options describe benefits, not disadvantages, of division of labour.
questions.p: Even though division of labour fit increase output and reduce cost, to dey repeat one same small work every day fit make worker tire and bore, and e fit reduce how dem dey work well. The other options na advantages, no be wahala.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa invests ₦500,000 of his own savings to start a poultry business. Unlike his workers who receive a fixed monthly wage regardless of the business outcome, Alhaji Musa bears the risk of losing his capital if the business fails. The reward he receives for bearing this risk and organising the business is called:
questions.e: Profit is the reward for the entrepreneur, who organises other factors of production and bears the risk of loss. Unlike wages (fixed payment for labour), interest (payment for capital) or rent (payment for land), profit is uncertain and depends on how well the business performs.
questions.p: Profit na the entrepreneur im reward, because na im dey organise everything and carry the risk of loss. E no be like wages (for labour), interest (for capital) or rent (for land) wey dem sure of; profit fit high or fit even no come at all.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes retail trade?
o: The production of goods for mass consumption
The sale of goods in bulk to other traders and wholesalers
The sale of goods and services directly to final consumers in small quantities
The exchange of goods between two different countries
questions.e: Retail trade is the last stage in the chain of distribution where goods are sold in small quantities directly to the final user. It does not involve bulk sales to other traders.
questions.p: Retail trade na the last stage wey trader dey sell goods small-small direct to the person wey go use am. E no be like wholesale wey dem dey sell plenty-plenty to other traders.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a large-scale retail organisation commonly found in big Nigerian cities?
questions.e: A department store is a large retail outlet with many departments selling different categories of goods under one roof, unlike hawkers, kiosks or market stalls which are small-scale.
questions.p: Department store na big shop wey get different sections wey dey sell different kind goods for one building. Hawker, kiosk and stall na small-small retail wey no reach that level.

questions.q: One major function of a retailer in the chain of distribution is to:
o: manufacture goods for sale to the public
fix the price of goods for the whole economy
control the foreign exchange rate of the country
break bulk goods from wholesalers into smaller units for consumers
questions.e: Retailers buy goods in fairly large quantities from wholesalers or manufacturers and break them into small units that ordinary consumers can afford, such as selling a bag of rice by the cup.
questions.p: Retailer dey buy plenty goods from wholesaler, then e go break am small-small so that ordinary buyer fit afford am, like how dem dey sell rice for cup instead of bag.

questions.q: A key feature that distinguishes a chain store (multiple shop) from a single independent retail shop is that a chain store:
o: is owned and controlled only by the government
does not offer any after-sales service to customers
operates several branches in different locations under one ownership and common policy
sells only one type of product in one location
questions.e: A chain store, also called a multiple shop, has several branches spread across different towns or cities, all owned by the same company and run under the same policies, prices and trademark. An independent shop has only one outlet.
questions.p: Chain store na business wey get many branches for different places, but one company dey own and control all of dem with same rules and price. Independent shop na just one branch alone.

questions.q: Mrs. Chidinma buys a sewing machine under a hire purchase agreement. The cash price is ₦15,000. She pays a deposit of 20% of the cash price, and then pays 10 equal monthly instalments of ₦1,500 each. What is the total amount she pays under the hire purchase agreement?
questions.e: Deposit = 20% of 15,000 = ₦3,000. Instalments = 10 x 1,500 = ₦15,000. Total hire purchase price = 3,000 + 15,000 = ₦18,000, which is more than the cash price because of the credit terms.
questions.p: Deposit na 20% of 15,000 wey be ₦3,000. The instalments na 10 x 1,500 wey be ₦15,000. If you add dem together, total na ₦18,000, e pass the cash price because of the credit arrangement.

questions.q: Why do many Nigerian supermarkets prefer the self-service method of selling goods?
o: It stops customers from seeing the goods before they pay for them
It reduces the cost of employing many sales attendants and speeds up shopping
It removes the need to display price tags on goods
It allows customers to bargain and reduce the price of goods freely
questions.e: Under self-service, customers pick goods themselves from shelves and pay at the checkout point, so the shop needs fewer sales attendants, which cuts labour cost and makes shopping faster.
questions.p: For self-service, customer dey pick the goods demsef from shelf and pay for counter, so the shop no go need plenty sales attendant. Dis one dey reduce cost and make shopping sharp-sharp.

questions.q: Which of the following goods is LEAST suitable for sale through mail order retailing (where customers order from a catalogue and goods are delivered by post or courier)?
questions.e: Mail order works best for goods that can survive transport delays without damage, like books, clothes and electronics. Perishable fresh fish can spoil before it reaches the buyer, making it unsuitable for this method.
questions.p: Mail order dey better pass for goods wey fit survive delay for road, like book, clothes and electronics. Fresh fish fit spoil before e reach the buyer, so e no good for mail order.

questions.q: One major function of the wholesaler is 'breaking bulk'. What does this mean?
o: Transporting goods from one country to another
Dividing large quantities of goods into smaller units for sale to retailers
Advertising goods on behalf of manufacturers
questions.e: Breaking bulk means the wholesaler buys goods in large quantities from producers and divides them into smaller, manageable quantities that retailers can afford to buy and store.
questions.p: Breaking bulk na when wholesaler buy plenty plenty goods from producer, then e go divide am into small small quantity wey retailer fit buy and keep.

questions.q: Which of the following is a service a wholesaler usually renders to retailers?
o: Collecting value added tax on behalf of government
Fixing the final selling price retailers must charge consumers
questions.e: Wholesalers often give retailers credit so they can stock goods and pay later after selling. This helps small retailers who may not have enough capital to pay cash immediately.
questions.p: Wholesaler dey often give retailer credit make e fit carry goods first and pay later after e don sell am. Na im dey help small retailer wey no get enough money pay cash.

questions.q: A type of wholesaler whose customers, usually small retailers, must pay in cash and carry their own goods away without any home delivery service is called a ____ wholesaler.
questions.e: A cash and carry wholesaler sells goods only for cash and does not deliver; buyers must arrange their own transport to carry goods away. This keeps the wholesaler's operating cost low.
questions.p: Cash and carry wholesaler na im be the one wey dey sell only for cash, e no dey deliver goods; na buyer go arrange how to carry im goods comot. Dis one dey make im cost low.

questions.q: Chief Nkemdirim, a wholesaler in Onitsha, bought 300 cartons of tomato paste at ₦12,000 per carton and later sold each carton to retailers at ₦17,000. What was his total profit on the 300 cartons?
questions.e: Profit per carton = 17,000 - 12,000 = 5,000. Total profit = 5,000 x 300 = 1,500,000. This shows how wholesalers earn their margin by buying in bulk and selling in smaller units at a higher price.
questions.p: Profit for one carton = 17,000 minus 12,000 = 5,000. Total profit = 5,000 times 300 = 1,500,000. Na so wholesaler dey make profit, e dey buy plenty cheap, e dey sell small expensive.

questions.q: A manufacturer is most likely to bypass the wholesaler and sell directly to retailers or consumers in which of these situations?
o: When the manufacturer wants to store goods for very long periods before selling
When the manufacturer has no means of transport to move goods
When the manufacturer produces a small range of perishable goods that need quick delivery to the market
When the manufacturer produces goods in very large quantities for many retailers scattered across the country
questions.e: Perishable goods like fresh bread or milk spoil quickly, so manufacturers sell directly and fast to retailers or consumers to avoid delay and loss caused by passing through a wholesaler. Non-perishable goods meant for many scattered retailers usually still need a wholesaler.
questions.p: Goods wey dey quick spoil like bread or fresh milk no get time to pass through wholesaler, so manufacturer go sell am sharp sharp direct to retailer or consumer make e no waste. Goods wey no dey spoil and wey plenty retailer dey scatter everywhere go still need wholesaler.

questions.q: A retailer bought an item from a wholesaler at a catalogue (list) price of ₦5,000 but was given a trade discount of 12%. How much did the retailer actually pay the wholesaler for the item?
questions.e: Trade discount = 12% of 5,000 = 600. Amount actually paid = 5,000 - 600 = 4,400. Trade discount is deducted from the catalogue price before the retailer pays, as a reward for buying from the wholesaler.
questions.p: Trade discount = 12% of 5,000 = 600. Wetin dem go pay = 5,000 minus 600 = 4,400. Dem dey remove trade discount from the catalogue price before retailer go pay, as appreciation for buying from wholesaler.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines foreign trade?
o: Buying and selling of goods within one country
Exchange of goods and services between two or more countries
Trade carried out only through barter
Trade limited to goods produced by government agencies
questions.e: Foreign trade simply means the exchange of goods and services across the borders of two or more countries, such as Nigeria trading with China or Ghana. Option A describes home trade, not foreign trade.
questions.p: Foreign trade na when goods and services dey exchange between two or more kontri, like Nigeria dey trade with China. Option A na just home trade, e no concern foreign trade.

questions.q: Which document serves as evidence of a contract of carriage of goods by sea, and also acts as a title (proof of ownership) to the goods being shipped?
questions.e: A bill of lading is issued by the shipping company to the exporter as proof that goods have been loaded on board a ship; it also acts as a document of title, so whoever holds it can claim the goods. The other documents serve different purposes like payment guarantee or origin declaration.
questions.p: Bill of lading na the paper wey show say goods don enter ship, and e dey also show say person wey hold am get right to the goods. The other papers dey do different work like payment or where goods come from.

questions.q: A trader in Kano wants to import packaged rice from Thailand. Which document will officially show the country where the rice was actually grown and processed?
questions.e: The certificate of origin is issued to state the country in which goods were produced or manufactured, which helps customs apply the correct duty or trade agreement rules. A bill of lading only shows that goods were shipped, not where they were made.
questions.p: Certificate of origin na the paper wey dey show the kontri wia dem produce the goods, e dey help custom know the correct duty to charge. Bill of lading na just show say dem don ship the goods, e no show wia e come from.

questions.q: Which of the following documents is issued by a bank to guarantee that an exporter will be paid once the agreed shipping documents are presented?
questions.e: A letter of credit is a bank's written guarantee of payment to the exporter once the required shipping documents, such as the bill of lading, are produced. This reduces the risk of non-payment in international trade, unlike a proforma invoice which is just a price quotation.
questions.p: Letter of credit na wetin bank dey give to promise say dem go pay the exporter once e bring the correct shipping papers. E dey reduce fear of no payment for foreign trade, unlike proforma invoice wey just dey show price.

questions.q: In foreign trade, which document does an importer complete and submit to the customs authorities to formally declare goods being brought into the country?
questions.e: A bill of entry is the official document an importer fills and submits to customs, declaring details such as the type, quantity and value of goods being imported, so that duty can be assessed. It is different from the bill of lading, which is a shipping document from the carrier.
questions.p: Bill of entry na the paper wey importer go fill give customs to declare the goods wey e dey bring enter kontri, so dem fit calculate duty. E different from bill of lading wey be shipping paper from the carrier.

questions.q: A Nigerian company agreed to buy machinery from Germany at a Free On Board (FOB) price of ₦500,000. The freight charge from Germany to Lagos port is ₦60,000, while the insurance premium on the goods is ₦15,000. What is the Cost, Insurance and Freight (CIF) price of the machinery?
questions.e: CIF price equals FOB price plus freight plus insurance: ₦500,000 + ₦60,000 + ₦15,000 = ₦575,000. CIF always includes all these costs up to the destination port, unlike FOB which stops at the point of loading.
questions.p: CIF price na FOB price add freight add insurance: 500,000 + 60,000 + 15,000 = 575,000. CIF dey cover everything reach the destination port, unlike FOB wey dey stop for where dem load the ship.

questions.q: In a particular trading year, Nigeria exported goods worth ₦2,400,000 and imported goods worth ₦1,850,000. What was Nigeria's balance of trade for that year?
questions.e: Balance of trade is calculated as total value of exports minus total value of imports: ₦2,400,000 - ₦1,850,000 = ₦550,000. Since exports are greater than imports, this is a surplus (favourable balance of trade).
questions.p: Balance of trade na export value minus import value: 2,400,000 - 1,850,000 = 550,000. Since export pass import, na surplus (favourable balance of trade) dem get.

questions.q: Chidinma runs a small provision store in Nnewi. She owns the business alone, takes all the profits, and is personally responsible for all debts if the business fails. What type of business unit is this?
questions.e: A sole proprietorship is owned and controlled by one person who enjoys all profits but also bears unlimited liability for debts. Chidinma's situation matches this exactly.
questions.p: Na one person dey run the business, e dey chop all the profit and e go pay all debt if the business fail. Na so sole proprietorship be.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major disadvantage of a sole proprietorship compared to a joint stock company?
o: It requires many legal documents to start
Its profit must be shared with many shareholders
It must publish its accounts yearly
It has limited capital for expansion
questions.e: A sole trader depends mostly on personal savings and small loans, so the business often lacks enough capital to expand, unlike companies that can raise funds from many shareholders. The other options describe features of companies, not sole proprietorships.
questions.p: Sole trader dey use im own money and small loan, so e no get plenty capital to expand pass companies wey fit raise money from shareholders. The other options na things wey concern company, no be sole trader.

questions.q: In a partnership business, what is the main legal document that states how profits and losses will be shared among the partners?
questions.e: The partnership deed (or partnership agreement) is the document that spells out how profits, losses, and duties are shared among partners. The other documents listed belong to registered companies, not partnerships.
questions.p: Na partnership deed dey show how dem go share profit and loss among the partners. The other papers na for company, no be partnership.

questions.q: Four friends in Ibadan want to start a business where each one's liability for business debts will be limited to the amount of capital they invested, and the business can continue to exist even if one of them dies. Which business unit best suits their need?
questions.e: A private limited liability company has a separate legal existence from its owners, so it does not end when a member dies, and shareholders' liability is limited to their shares. A general partnership does not automatically give limited liability to all partners.
questions.p: Private limited company get im own legal identity wey no go end when one owner die, and the liability na only to how much capital dem put. General partnership no dey give automatic limited liability like that.

questions.q: A cooperative society in Benue State wants to raise money for its members to buy farm inputs at a cheaper rate and share any surplus based on how much business each member did with the society, not on shares owned. Which principle of cooperative societies does this describe?
questions.e: Cooperative societies share surplus (profit) according to the amount of business (patronage) each member transacted with the society, not according to shares held, which is different from how companies pay dividends. This encourages members to use the cooperative's services more.
questions.p: Cooperative society dey share surplus based on how much business the member do with am, no be how much share e hold. Na so e dey encourage members to patronize the cooperative well well.

questions.q: A partnership in Kano has three partners: Musa contributed capital only and takes no part in management, while Bala and Yusuf manage the business daily and also contributed capital. What type of partner is Musa?
questions.e: A sleeping (dormant) partner contributes capital and shares profits but does not take part in the daily management of the business, exactly like Musa. An active or general partner, by contrast, is involved in running the business.
questions.p: Sleeping partner na im put money but e no dey involve for daily running of the business, just like Musa. Active or general partner dey help run the business every day.

questions.q: A joint stock company in Lagos has 50,000 ordinary shares of ₦20 each fully subscribed and paid for. If the company declares a total dividend of ₦250,000 for the year, what is the dividend paid per share?
questions.e: Total dividend divided by number of shares gives dividend per share: 250,000 / 50,000 = ₦5.00 per share. The ₦20 price of each share is not needed for this calculation since dividend is shared equally per share, not based on share price alone in this question.
questions.p: You go divide total dividend by number of shares: 250,000 / 50,000 = ₦5.00 for each share. The ₦20 wey be price of share no relevant here, na per-share calculation.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a function of money?
questions.e: Money works as a medium of exchange, a store of value, and a standard for deferred payment. Creating employment is the work of businesses, government and investment, not a function of money itself.
questions.p: Money dey help as medium of exchange, store of value, and standard for deferred payment. But to create employment na work for business and government, e no be function of money.

questions.q: Which bank in Nigeria is known as the banker to the government and to other banks, and also controls the nation's money supply?
questions.e: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) acts as banker to the government and to commercial banks, issues currency, and controls money supply through monetary policy. Commercial, merchant and microfinance banks serve the public, not the government or other banks.
questions.p: Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) na banker to government and to the other banks, e dey control how much money dey circulate. Commercial, merchant and microfinance banks dey serve ordinary customers, not government or other banks.

questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of good money?
questions.e: Good money must be divisible into smaller units so it can be used for both large and small transactions. Money that perishes quickly, is heavy to carry, or has irregular supply cannot serve its purpose well.
questions.p: Good money suppose divisible well-well so e fit use for big and small transaction. Money wey dey spoil quick, wey heavy to carry, or wey no dey available well no good as money.

questions.q: A commercial bank receives an initial deposit of ₦50,000 from a customer. If the Central Bank's required cash reserve ratio is 20%, what is the maximum total deposits the banking system can create from this initial deposit, assuming the credit multiplier process runs fully?
questions.e: The credit multiplier is 1 divided by the reserve ratio, which is 1/0.20 = 5. Maximum total deposits = initial deposit x multiplier = 50,000 x 5 = ₦250,000.
questions.p: Credit multiplier na 1 divide by reserve ratio, wey be 1/0.20 = 5. So maximum total deposit = 50,000 x 5 = ₦250,000.

questions.q: Which of these financial instruments is mainly used by a current account holder to withdraw money from the bank over the counter?
questions.e: A cheque is a written order used by a current account holder to instruct the bank to pay out cash or transfer money. A promissory note, bill of exchange, and dividend warrant serve other purposes such as credit agreements or share payments.
questions.p: Cheque na written instruction wey current account owner dey use tell bank make dem pay cash or transfer money. Promissory note, bill of exchange and dividend warrant get different use, no be for counter withdrawal.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes inflation?
o: A persistent rise in the general price level
A fall in the interest rate charged by banks
A persistent fall in the general price level
A rise in the exchange rate of the naira
questions.e: Inflation is a continuous and general increase in the prices of goods and services over time, which reduces the purchasing power of money. A fall in prices is deflation, not inflation.
questions.p: Inflation na when price of goods and services dey rise rise continuously, e dey reduce wetin money fit buy. If price dey fall, na deflation, no be inflation.

questions.q: Mrs. Chiamaka Okafor borrowed ₦120,000 from her cooperative society at a simple interest rate of 15% per annum for 2 years. Calculate the total amount she will repay at the end of the loan period.
questions.e: Simple interest = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100 = (120,000 x 15 x 2)/100 = ₦36,000. Total repayment = Principal + Interest = 120,000 + 36,000 = ₦156,000.
questions.p: Simple interest = (Principal x Rate x Time)/100 = (120,000 x 15 x 2)/100 = ₦36,000. Total wey she go pay back = 120,000 + 36,000 = ₦156,000.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the Nigerian Stock Exchange?
o: A government agency that fixes prices of goods
An organized market for buying and selling existing stocks and shares
A market for buying and selling second-hand goods
A place where only newly registered companies hold their first meeting
questions.e: The stock exchange is a formal, organized market where existing shares, stocks and other securities are bought and sold. It is not about second-hand goods or price control.
questions.p: Stock exchange na proper organized market where people dey buy and sell shares wey don already dey exist. E no concern second-hand goods or price control.

questions.q: A document issued to an investor as proof that he/she owns a stated number of shares in a company is called a:
questions.e: A share certificate is the official document that shows how many shares a person owns in a company. The other documents listed are used in transport, borrowing and insurance matters, not ownership of shares.
questions.p: Share certificate na di paper wey show say person get shares for one company. Di other documents na for transport, borrowing or insurance, dem no concern share ownership.

questions.q: The capital market, unlike the money market, mainly provides funds for:
o: Short-term needs such as treasury bills
Long-term needs such as shares and debentures
questions.e: The capital market deals with long-term financial instruments like shares and debentures used to finance long-term business projects, while the money market handles short-term instruments like treasury bills.
questions.p: Capital market na for long-term funds like shares and debentures wey business dey use for long-term projects. Na money market dey handle short-term things like treasury bills.

questions.q: Mr. Danjuma works for a licensed firm that buys and sells shares on the stock exchange on behalf of clients, earning commission on each transaction. Mr. Danjuma is best described as a:
questions.e: A stockbroker is a licensed agent who buys and sells shares for clients on the stock exchange and earns commission. A registrar keeps shareholders' records, an issuing house helps float new shares, and a trustee manages property for beneficiaries.
questions.p: Stockbroker na di licensed person wey dey buy and sell shares for client for stock exchange and e dey collect commission. Registrar na di one wey dey keep shareholders record, issuing house dey help float new shares, trustee dey manage property for beneficiary.

questions.q: When a company sells its shares to the public for the very first time through the stock exchange machinery, this activity takes place in the:
o: Buying and selling of existing shares only
Trading of commodities like cocoa and palm oil
questions.e: The new issues market, also called the primary market, is where companies sell new shares or debentures to the public for the first time to raise fresh capital. The secondary market is where existing shares already issued are later traded among investors.
questions.p: New issues market (primary market) na where company dey sell new shares to public for di first time to raise money. Na secondary market dem dey use trade shares wey don already dey circulate.

questions.q: A share of Zenith Textile Plc is quoted on the stock exchange at ₦25.00 per share. The company pays an annual dividend of ₦2.50 per share. Calculate the dividend yield on the share.
questions.e: Dividend yield = (Dividend per share / Market price per share) x 100 = (2.50/25) x 100 = 10%. This tells an investor the return they get from dividends relative to the share's market price.
questions.p: Dividend yield = (Dividend per share / Market price) x 100 = (2.50/25) x 100 = 10%. Na im dey show how much return investor dey get from dividend compare to di share price.

questions.q: Chidi has ₦60,000.00 which he wants to invest in shares quoted on the stock exchange at ₦30.00 per share. How many shares can he buy with this amount, ignoring any brokerage fees?
questions.e: Number of shares = Total amount available / Price per share = 60,000 / 30 = 2000 shares. Brokerage fees are ignored, so the full amount is used to calculate the number of shares.
questions.p: Number of shares = Total money / Price per share = 60,000 / 30 = 2000 shares. Dem no add brokerage fee, so na di full money dem use calculate di shares.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines insurance?
o: A government scheme for distributing relief materials to disaster victims
A contract where one party agrees to pay premium only when loss occurs
A saving scheme where money is kept with a bank for future use
A contract where the insurer agrees to compensate the insured against unforeseen loss in exchange for a premium
questions.e: Insurance is a contract in which the insurer promises to pay compensation for a specified loss in return for regular payment called premium. It is not a savings scheme or a government relief programme.
questions.p: Insurance na agreement wia di insurance company go pay you compensation if loss happen, as you dey pay premium regularly. E no be savings or government relief matter.

questions.q: The principle of insurance which requires a person taking out a policy to disclose all material facts about the risk to be insured is called:
questions.e: Utmost good faith (uberrimae fidei) demands that both the insurer and the insured disclose all relevant facts honestly before and during the contract. Hiding facts can make the policy void.
questions.p: Utmost good faith mean say both di insurance company and di person wey dey insure must tell true true, no hide anything about di risk. If you hide am, di policy fit no work.

questions.q: Chidi insures a warehouse that he neither owns nor has any financial stake in. Which principle of insurance does this situation violate?
questions.e: Insurable interest means the insured must have a legal or financial relationship with the item insured so that its loss would cause him financial harm. Since Chidi has no stake in the warehouse, he lacks insurable interest.
questions.p: Insurable interest mean say di person wey insure something must get financial connection to am, so dat if e spoil e go lose money. Chidi no get any stake for dat warehouse, so e no get insurable interest.

questions.q: Mr. Bello insures his shop goods valued at ₦500,000 against fire at a premium rate of 2.5% of the value insured. How much premium will he pay?
questions.e: Premium = 2.5% of ₦500,000 = 0.025 x 500,000 = ₦12,500. This is the amount Mr. Bello must pay the insurer for the cover.
questions.p: Premium na 2.5% of ₦500,000 = 0.025 x 500,000 = ₦12,500. Na dis amount Mr. Bello go pay to insurance company.

questions.q: Mrs. Adeyemi insures her shop stock valued at ₦1,000,000 for only ₦600,000. A fire outbreak later destroys stock worth ₦300,000. Applying the average clause (under-insurance principle), how much will the insurance company pay her?
questions.e: Under the average clause, compensation = (Sum Insured / Actual Value) x Loss = (600,000/1,000,000) x 300,000 = ₦180,000. Because she under-insured, she bears part of the loss herself.
questions.p: Average clause mean say dem go pay you based on how much you insure compared to di real value: (600,000/1,000,000) x 300,000 = ₦180,000. Since she under-insure, she go carry part of di loss herself.

questions.q: A factory valued at ₦2,000,000 is insured with two different companies: Company X covers ₦800,000 and Company Y covers ₦1,200,000. A fire causes damage amounting to ₦400,000. Applying the principle of contribution, how much will Company X pay?
questions.e: Under contribution, each insurer pays in proportion to its share of the total cover. Company X's share = (800,000/2,000,000) x 400,000 = ₦160,000, preventing the insured from profiting from double insurance.
questions.p: Contribution mean say each insurance company go pay based on how much dem cover. Company X go pay (800,000/2,000,000) x 400,000 = ₦160,000, so dat person no go gain extra money from double insurance.

questions.q: In Nigeria, which body is responsible for regulating and supervising the activities of insurance companies?
questions.e: NAICOM (National Insurance Commission) is the statutory body charged with regulating, supervising and controlling insurance business in Nigeria, while CBN handles banks and SEC handles the capital market.
questions.p: NAICOM na di government body wey dey regulate and supervise insurance business for Nigeria, while CBN dey handle banks and SEC dey handle capital market.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major mode of transport used in Nigeria for moving goods and people?
questions.e: Road transport is one of the main ways of moving goods and people from one place to another. Banking, insurance and warehousing are aids to trade, not modes of transport.
questions.p: Road transport na one of the main way wey dem dey use carry goods and people go anywhere. Banking, insurance and warehousing na aids to trade, dem no be transport.

questions.q: A document issued by a shipping company to acknowledge that goods have been received on board a ship for carriage to another port is called a
questions.e: A bill of lading is the document a shipping company gives as proof that goods have been loaded on a ship for sea transport. A waybill is used for road or rail transport, while an invoice shows price details, and a charter party is a contract for hiring a whole ship.
questions.p: Bill of lading na the paper wey shipping company dey give as proof say dem don load goods inside ship for sea transport. Waybill na for road or rail, invoice na for price, charter party na contract to hire whole ship.

questions.q: Which of these is the most suitable mode of transport for moving crude oil from an oil field to a refinery over a long distance?
questions.e: Pipelines are specially built to carry liquids and gases such as crude oil, petrol and water over long distances continuously and cheaply. Road, rail and air transport are not designed for bulk liquid movement like this.
questions.p: Pipeline na the one wey dem dey build specially to carry liquid and gas like crude oil, petrol and water for far distance, e cheap well well. Road, rail and air no fit carry plenty liquid like that.

questions.q: A trader in Onitsha hires a lorry to carry her goods to Lagos. The transport company charges ₦500 per kg for the first 50kg and ₦300 per kg for every additional kg above 50kg. If her load weighs 80kg, how much will she pay in total?
questions.p: First 50kg na 50 x 500 = 25,000 naira. The remaining 30kg (80 minus 50) na 30 x 300 = 9,000 naira. Add dem together you go get 34,000 naira.

questions.q: In sea transport, the extra charge paid by an importer when his ship is delayed beyond the agreed loading or unloading time at a port is called
questions.e: Demurrage is the penalty charge paid when a ship stays longer than the agreed time at the port for loading or unloading. Freight is the normal charge for carrying goods, while premium and commission relate to insurance and selling agents respectively.
questions.p: Demurrage na the extra money wey dem go pay if ship stay pass the time wey dem agree for port to load or unload. Freight na the normal charge to carry goods, premium na insurance money and commission na agent payment.

questions.q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of air transport compared to road transport in Nigeria?
o: It is faster for long distances
It cannot be used for perishable goods
It is cheaper for bulky goods over short distances
It requires heavy capital investment and high operating cost
questions.e: Air transport needs expensive aircraft, airports and trained staff, making it very costly to set up and run. It is actually fast and good for perishable goods, but not cheap for bulky, short-distance loads, which makes options A, B and C wrong.
questions.p: Air transport need expensive aeroplane, airport and trained workers, so e cost plenty money to start and run. E dey fast and e good for perishable goods, but e no cheap for heavy load wey dey travel short distance, so the other options no correct.

questions.q: A carrier's right to hold on to a customer's goods until the agreed transport charges have been fully paid is known as
questions.e: A carrier's lien is the legal right of a transporter to keep goods until the owner pays the agreed transport charges. A freight note shows the amount charged, a consignment note describes the goods being sent, and way leave refers to permission to lay pipelines or cables across land.
questions.p: Carrier's lien na the right wey transporter get to hold goods until owner pay the transport money wey dem agree. Freight note na paper wey show the charge, consignment note na paper wey describe the goods, way leave na permission to lay pipe or cable pass land.

questions.q: In Commerce, the process by which information, ideas and feelings are exchanged between a sender and a receiver through an agreed channel is known as what?
questions.e: Communication is the exchange of information, ideas or feelings between a sender and a receiver using a channel. Negotiation, advertising and distribution are different business activities, not the process of exchanging messages.
questions.p: Communication na the process where person dey send message give another person and e understand am. Negotiation, advertising and distribution na different business things wey no be message exchange.

questions.q: In the communication process, the person to whom a message is sent and who interprets it is referred to as the?
questions.e: The receiver is the person who gets the message and decodes (interprets) it. The sender originates the message, the medium carries it, and feedback is the receiver's response back to the sender.
questions.p: The receiver na the person wey the message dey go meet and e go understand the meaning. Sender na the one wey start the message, medium na the way e pass through, feedback na reply wey receiver give back.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a barrier to effective communication in a business office?
questions.e: Clear feedback shows that a message has been well understood, so it is a sign of effective communication, not a barrier. Noise, language difference and poor network can all distort or block a message.
questions.p: Clear feedback mean say message don enter well, na sign say communication succeed, e no be barrier. Noise, language difference and poor network fit spoil or block the message.

questions.q: Mr. Adeyemi, a trader in Kano, needs to send an urgent short message to his supplier in Lagos and get an immediate reply on the price of goods. Which means of communication is most suitable for him?
questions.e: The telephone allows two-way, instant exchange of messages over a long distance, so Mr. Adeyemi can get an immediate reply. Newspaper and radio are for public announcements, while a letter by post would take too long for an urgent reply.
questions.p: Telephone dey allow person talk and hear reply immediately even if the distance far, so na the best one for urgent matter. Newspaper and radio na for public announcement, letter by post go slow reach.

questions.q: The informal and unofficial channel through which information, including rumours, spreads quickly among workers in an organisation is called the?
questions.e: The grapevine is the informal network through which information, gossip and rumours move among employees outside official channels. Vertical and horizontal communication describe formal direction of flow, while a memorandum is a formal written note.
questions.p: Grapevine na the informal way wey gist and news dey waka pass among workers outside official line. Vertical and horizontal communication na formal direction, memorandum na formal written note.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major advantage of oral communication over written communication in a business setting?
o: It is more expensive to use
It eliminates distortion of the message
questions.e: Oral communication, such as face-to-face talk or phone calls, allows the receiver to respond at once, so the sender gets immediate feedback. Written communication, not oral, provides a permanent record, and oral messages can actually be more easily distorted, not less.
questions.p: Oral communication like phone call or face-to-face talk dey allow person reply sharp sharp, so feedback dey come immediately. Na written communication dey provide permanent record, and oral message fit still distort pass written one.

questions.q: A factory manager complains that the workers often misunderstand the written instructions he sends because the memo is full of technical terms they are not familiar with. This communication problem is best described as a barrier caused by?
questions.e: The problem arises because the words (technical jargon) used are not understood by the workers, which is a language barrier. It is not noise (physical disturbance), distance, or poor timing, since the memo was written and delivered, but its wording caused confusion.
questions.p: The wahala na because the grammar wey the manager use (technical words) no clear to the workers, na language barrier be dat. E no be noise, distance or poor timing wey cause am, na the wording wey confuse dem.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines advertising?
o: A paid form of non-personal communication about goods and services aimed at a target audience
The process of packaging goods for sale in the market
A face-to-face discussion between a seller and a single buyer
The physical movement of goods from the factory to the warehouse
questions.e: Advertising is a paid, non-personal way of informing or persuading people about goods and services. It is not direct personal selling, transportation, or packaging.
questions.p: Advertising na paid message wey no be face-to-face, e dey tell people about goods and services. E no be personal selling, transport, or packaging.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a function of advertising?
o: Setting the exact market price that all sellers must charge
Reminding consumers of an existing brand
Creating awareness of a new product
questions.e: Advertising informs, educates, and reminds consumers, but it does not fix or control the exact price every seller must charge. Pricing decisions are separate from the advertising function.
questions.p: Advertising dey create awareness, educate and remind people about product, but e no dey fix the exact price wey all sellers go charge. Pricing na different matter from advertising.

questions.q: A manufacturer of bottled drinks in Kano wants an advertising medium that can combine sound, pictures, and movement to demonstrate how the drink is poured and enjoyed, reaching millions of households at once. Which medium is most suitable?
questions.e: Television combines sound, moving pictures, and wide reach, making it ideal for demonstrating a product dynamically to many households. Handbills, newspapers, and posters are static and cannot show movement or sound.
questions.p: Television get sound, moving pictures and e dey reach plenty houses, so e good well-well to show how to pour and enjoy the drink. Handbill, newspaper and poster no fit show movement or make sound.

questions.q: A new biscuit company spends heavily on advertising but experiences only a small, temporary rise in sales because most consumers in the area already have strong brand loyalty to an older, well-established biscuit brand. This situation best illustrates which limitation of advertising?
o: Advertising automatically reduces the price of the advertised product
Advertising is illegal when a stronger competitor exists in the market
Advertising can create brand awareness but cannot force consumers to abandon strong existing brand loyalty
Advertising always guarantees an immediate large increase in sales
questions.e: Advertising can inform people about a product, but it cannot force consumers to switch from a brand they are already strongly loyal to; change in buying habits often takes more time and other strategies. The other options are false statements about advertising.
questions.p: Advertising fit tell people about product, but e no fit force people to comot from brand wey dem don already dey loyal to; to change people mind fit take time and other strategy. The other options no correct at all.

questions.q: In Commerce, warehousing simply means the:
o: process of buying goods in bulk and selling in bits
act of transporting goods from producer to consumer
advertising of goods to attract customers
storage of goods in a safe place until they are needed
questions.e: Warehousing is the holding or keeping of goods safely in a store until they are required for sale or use. It is different from transporting, buying/selling in bits, or advertising, which are other trade activities.
questions.p: Warehousing na to keep goods well-well for one safe place until the time wey dem go need am. E no be about carry goods go buyer, buy-and-sell for small-small, or to advertise goods.

questions.q: A type of warehouse where imported goods are kept under the watch of customs officers, and import duty is not paid until the goods are released for sale, is called a ___ warehouse.
questions.e: A bonded warehouse is controlled by customs officials and holds imported goods until the importer pays the required duty before release. This is different from private, public or cold storage warehouses, which do not focus on duty collection.
questions.p: Bonded warehouse na the one wey customs people dey control, and dem no go collect duty until the importer wan release the goods. E different from private, public or cold storage warehouse.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the importance of warehousing to trade?
o: It reduces the quality of goods that are stored
It increases the price of goods immediately they are produced
It helps to bridge the time gap between production and consumption
It makes goods available only during periods of scarcity
questions.e: Warehousing allows goods produced at one time to be stored and made available later when consumers need them, thereby linking production time with consumption time. It does not necessarily raise prices or reduce quality.
questions.p: Warehousing dey help connect the time wey dem produce goods and the time wey people go need am, so e dey fill the gap between production and when people go buy am. E no be say e go automatically raise price or spoil the goods.

questions.q: The document issued by a warehouse keeper to show that specific goods have been deposited in the warehouse, and which can also be used to transfer ownership of the goods to another person, is called a:
questions.e: A warehouse warrant is proof that goods are stored in a named warehouse, and it can be endorsed to another person to transfer ownership without moving the goods physically. A bill of lading covers sea transport, an invoice is a bill for goods sold, and a certificate of origin shows where goods were produced.
questions.p: Warehouse warrant na the paper wey show say dem don keep particular goods for warehouse, and you fit sign am give another person to transfer ownership. Bill of lading na for sea transport, invoice na bill for goods wey dem sell, and certificate of origin na for where dem produce the goods.

questions.q: What is a major advantage of a bonded warehouse to an importer who is not yet ready to sell his imported goods?
o: He must sell the goods within 24 hours of arrival
He can store the goods and delay payment of duty until he is ready to release them
He pays import duty in full before his goods can be stored
He automatically loses ownership of the goods to the government
questions.e: A bonded warehouse allows an importer to keep goods safely without paying duty immediately, only paying when the goods are actually released for sale. This gives the importer time and reduces pressure to sell quickly or raise money for duty at once.
questions.p: Bonded warehouse dey allow importer keep im goods well without paying duty sharp-sharp; e go only pay duty when e wan release the goods for market. This one dey give am time and e no go rush sell the goods or rush find money for duty.

questions.q: Mrs. Chioma stored 180 crates of soft drinks in a public warehouse in Onitsha. The warehouse charges ₦25 per crate for the first 4 weeks, and ₦10 per crate for each additional week after that. If she left the crates in the warehouse for a total of 6 weeks, how much rent did she pay altogether?
questions.e: First charge: 180 crates x ₦25 = ₦4,500 for the first 4 weeks. Extra weeks = 6 - 4 = 2 weeks, so extra charge = 180 x ₦10 x 2 = ₦3,600. Total rent = ₦4,500 + ₦3,600 = ₦8,100.
questions.p: First charge: 180 crates x ₦25 = ₦4,500 for the first 4 weeks. The extra weeks na 6 minus 4 = 2 weeks, so extra money = 180 x ₦10 x 2 = ₦3,600. Add dem together: ₦4,500 + ₦3,600 = ₦8,100.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa owns a large rice mill and built his own storage facility only to keep his company's bags of rice before they are sent out to his regular distributors. This type of warehouse is best described as a:
questions.e: A private warehouse is owned and used by one business solely for storing its own goods, as in Alhaji Musa's case. A public warehouse serves many different businesses, a bonded warehouse is for duty-unpaid imports, and a government warehouse belongs to the state.
questions.p: Private warehouse na the one wey one company build and use only for im own goods, like wetin Alhaji Musa do. Public warehouse na for many different businesses, bonded warehouse na for imported goods wey duty never pay, and government warehouse na property of government.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a middleman in trade?
o: A person or firm that stands between the producer and the final consumer in the distribution of goods
A government agency that regulates prices of goods
An insurance company that covers business risks
A bank that provides loans to producers
questions.e: A middleman is anyone who links the producer to the final consumer in the chain of distribution, such as a wholesaler, retailer or agent. Banks, government price agencies and insurance companies do not perform this linking role.
questions.p: Middleman na person or firm wey dey between the producer and the person wey go finally use the goods, e.g wholesaler or retailer. Bank, government price agency and insurance company no dey do this kain work.

questions.q: Which of these is classified as an aid to trade rather than a middleman?
questions.e: Warehousing is a service that supports trade by storing goods, so it is an aid to trade, not a middleman. Wholesalers, retailers and commission agents are middlemen because they stand between producers and consumers and take part in buying and selling.
questions.p: Warehousing na service wey dey help trade by storing goods, so e be aid to trade, e no be middleman. Wholesaler, retailer and commission agent na middlemen because dem dey buy and sell between producer and consumer.

questions.q: One major function of a wholesaler in the chain of distribution is to
o: manufacture goods in bulk for sale
insure goods against loss during production
advertise products directly to final consumers only
buy in bulk from producers and sell in smaller quantities to retailers
questions.e: A wholesaler buys goods in large quantities directly from producers and breaks them into smaller lots to sell to retailers. The wholesaler does not manufacture goods, and advertising to final consumers and insuring goods are not his core function.
questions.p: Wholesaler dey buy plenty goods straight from producer, then e go break am small small sell am to retailer. Wholesaler no dey manufacture goods, and e no be im job to advertise to final consumer or insure goods.

questions.q: Mr. Adeyemi negotiates the sale of goods between a textile producer in Kano and a trader in Onitsha but never takes ownership of the goods and earns a commission for each deal. Mr. Adeyemi is best described as a(n)
questions.e: A broker brings buyer and seller together and earns a commission but does not take possession or ownership of the goods, which matches Mr. Adeyemi's role exactly. A wholesaler and retailer actually buy and own the goods, while a del credere agent takes on the risk of bad debts for the goods he handles.
questions.p: Broker na im dey bring buyer and seller together make dem agree, e dey collect commission but e no dey own the goods, na so Mr. Adeyemi work be. Wholesaler and retailer dey actually buy and own goods, while del credere agent dey carry the risk if buyer no pay.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a function of warehousing as an aid to trade?
o: Providing a steady supply of goods throughout the year
Storing goods until they are needed by the market
Protecting goods from damage and deterioration
questions.e: Warehousing deals with storage, protection and steady supply of goods, not with lending money, which is the function of banks. Therefore granting loans is not a function of warehousing.
questions.p: Warehousing na about storing, protecting and making sure say goods dey available throughout the year, e no be about lending money, na bank dey do dat one. So granting loan no be warehousing function.

questions.q: A manufacturer of soft drinks in Lagos decides to sell directly to final consumers through his own retail shops, removing wholesalers and retailers from his distribution chain. Which of the following is a likely disadvantage of this decision?
o: Consumers will receive goods at a higher quality standard than before
The manufacturer will need to set up and manage many retail outlets himself, increasing his workload and capital requirement
The manufacturer will enjoy reduced cost of distribution immediately
Middlemen will automatically earn higher profits from the new arrangement
questions.e: When a manufacturer removes middlemen, he must now perform their storage, transport and selling functions himself, which means setting up many shops and spending more capital and effort. Product quality does not automatically improve, distribution costs usually rise at first rather than fall, and middlemen who are removed earn nothing from the new system.
questions.p: If manufacturer remove middlemen, e go need to do the work wey dem dey do before, like storage, transport and selling, so e go need open plenty shop and spend more money and energy. Quality no go automatically improve, cost go first rise instead of reduce, and the middlemen wey don comot no go earn anything again.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa owns a textile warehouse in Kano. He wants to protect his stock against loss from fire outbreak and also wants funds to expand his business without using his personal savings. Which two aids to trade will directly help him achieve these needs respectively?
questions.e: Insurance covers his stock against losses like fire outbreak, while banking provides loans and credit facilities for business expansion. Transportation, advertising, communication and warehousing serve other purposes such as moving goods, promoting sales and storage, not covering fire risk or providing expansion funds.
questions.p: Insurance go cover im goods if fire burn am, while bank go give am loan make e expand business without im savings. Transportation, advertising, communication and warehousing dey do other things like carry goods, advertise or store goods, dem no dey cover fire risk or give expansion money.

questions.q: In Commerce, what is the main meaning of 'consumer protection'?
o: A method used by firms to calculate the cost of production
Measures put in place to safeguard buyers from exploitation by producers and sellers
A government plan to increase taxes on imported goods
A policy that allows sellers to fix prices without control
questions.e: Consumer protection refers to all the laws, agencies and actions set up to protect buyers from being cheated, harmed or exploited by sellers and producers. The other options describe unrelated business or tax activities.
questions.p: Consumer protection na all the laws and actions wey dem use protect buyers from sellers wey wan cheat dem. The other options na about tax and pricing wey no concern protection of buyer.

questions.q: Which government agency in Nigeria is mainly responsible for checking that food and drugs sold to the public are safe for consumption?
o: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)
questions.e: NAFDAC is the agency charged with regulating and controlling the quality, safety and sale of food, drugs and related products in Nigeria. The other bodies deal with tax collection, stock trading and banking, not product safety.
questions.p: NAFDAC na the agency wey dey check say food and drugs wey dem dey sell for Nigeria safe for people. The other agencies dey handle tax, shares and banking, no be product safety.

questions.q: One basic right that consumer protection gives to a buyer is the right to
o: control how a factory produces its goods
fix the selling price of any product he buys
determine how much profit a trader should make
be heard and have his complaints addressed when a product is faulty
questions.e: Consumer protection guarantees the buyer the right to complain and be listened to when a product does not meet expectation or is defective. Fixing prices, profits or production belongs to the seller or producer, not the buyer.
questions.p: Consumer get right to complain and make dem hear am when product bad or no correct. To fix price, profit or production na seller or producer work, no be buyer own.

questions.q: The Latin saying 'let the buyer beware', which warns consumers to examine goods carefully before buying, is known as
questions.e: Caveat emptor is the Latin phrase meaning 'let the buyer beware', reminding consumers to inspect goods before purchase since protection may be limited. Caveat venditor means 'let the seller beware', while bona fide and ad valorem are unrelated commercial terms.
questions.p: Caveat emptor na Latin wey mean 'make buyer dey careful' before e buy something. Caveat venditor mean make seller dey careful, while bona fide and ad valorem na different business terms entirely.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a genuine method of protecting consumers in the marketplace?
o: Allowing advertisers to exaggerate product benefits without proof
Making laws against the adulteration of goods
Standardizing weights and measures used by traders
Forming consumer associations to handle collective complaints
questions.e: Allowing false or exaggerated advertising actually harms consumers instead of protecting them, so it is not a genuine protection method. Standardizing measures, forming associations and anti-adulteration laws are all real consumer protection measures.
questions.p: To allow advert wey dey lie or exaggerate go harm consumer instead of protect am, so e no be real protection method. The other three na correct ways wey dem dey use protect consumer.

questions.q: Mrs. Adaeze bought a bag of rice labelled 50kg, but when she weighed it at home, it measured only 45kg. Which Nigerian agency is most relevant in addressing this kind of consumer problem?
questions.e: SON is responsible for setting and enforcing standard weights, measures and quality for goods sold in Nigeria, so a short-weight bag of rice falls under its duty. The other agencies deal with copyright, ports operations and pensions, which are unrelated.
questions.p: SON na the agency wey dey make sure say weight and measure of goods correct, so rice wey no reach 50kg na dia work. Di oda agencies dey handle copyright, port and pension matter, no be weight wahala.

questions.q: A trader sells used (fairly used) phones to customers without telling them the phones are not brand new, so buyers pay prices meant for new phones. Which consumer right has been most directly violated?
o: Right to a clean and safe environment
Right to choose from a variety of goods
Right to representation in government policy
Right to accurate information about the product
questions.e: By hiding the true condition of the phones, the trader denies buyers correct information needed to make an informed decision, which directly violates the right to information. Choice, political representation and environmental rights are not the issue described here.
questions.p: The trader hide the true condition of the phone from buyer, so e don break the right to correct information wey go help buyer decide well. The other rights no match wetin dey happen for this story.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa sells building materials in Kano. After supplying goods to a customer, he sends a document showing the names and quantities of goods, the unit price and the total amount the customer must pay before payment is made. What is this document called?
questions.e: An invoice is issued by a seller to a buyer before payment, showing details of goods sold, quantity, price and the total amount due. A receipt is only given after payment has been made.
questions.p: Invoice na di paper wey seller give buyer before e pay, e dey show the goods, quantity, price and total wey e go pay. Receipt na wetin dem dey give after payment don happen.

questions.q: Mrs. Adaeze bought 20 bags of rice from a supplier, but when the goods arrived, 3 bags were damaged. She returned the damaged bags. Which document will the supplier send to her to show that the amount she owes has been reduced because of the returned goods?
questions.e: A credit note is issued by a seller to a buyer to reduce (credit) the amount owed when goods are returned or there has been an overcharge. A debit note works the other way, to increase the amount owed.
questions.p: Credit note na wetin seller dey send give buyer make im reduce the money wey e owe because goods don come back. Debit note na the one wey dey increase the money wey person owe.

questions.q: A furniture dealer in Onitsha marks a set of chairs at a list price of ₦15,000 and allows a trade discount of 20% to a retailer who buys in bulk. How much will the retailer actually pay?
questions.e: Trade discount is 20% of ₦15,000 = ₦3,000. The retailer pays the list price minus the discount: ₦15,000 - ₦3,000 = ₦12,000.
questions.p: Trade discount na 20% of ₦15,000 wey be ₦3,000. So wetin retailer go pay na ₦15,000 minus ₦3,000 wey be ₦12,000.

questions.q: Chidinma bought goods worth ₦40,000 from a wholesaler on the terms "5% cash discount if payment is made within 10 days". She paid the full amount on the 8th day. How much did she actually pay?
questions.e: Cash discount is 5% of ₦40,000 = ₦2,000. Since she paid within the 10-day period, she deducts this discount: ₦40,000 - ₦2,000 = ₦38,000.
questions.p: Cash discount na 5% of ₦40,000 wey be ₦2,000. Since she pay before the 10 days finish, she go minus the discount: ₦40,000 - ₦2,000 = ₦38,000.

questions.q: When goods are being transported from a seller's warehouse in Lagos to a buyer in Ibadan, which business document travels with the goods to show the driver and the receiving store the details and quantity of items being conveyed?
questions.e: A waybill accompanies goods during transportation and lists the items, quantity and destination, so the carrier and receiver can confirm what is being delivered. It is different from an invoice, which is about billing for payment.
questions.p: Waybill na the paper wey dey follow goods as dem dey carry am go, e dey show the items, quantity and where e dey go. E different from invoice wey be about money wey person go pay.

questions.q: A wholesaler sells goods listed at ₦50,000 to a retailer. The wholesaler allows a trade discount of 10% for buying in bulk, and a further cash discount of 5% if payment is made within 14 days. If the retailer pays within 14 days, how much does he pay in total?
questions.e: First deduct trade discount: ₦50,000 x 0.9 = ₦45,000. Then deduct cash discount on this new amount: ₦45,000 x 0.95 = ₦42,750. Trade discount is always applied first, then cash discount on the reduced price.
questions.p: First remove trade discount: ₦50,000 x 0.9 = ₦45,000. Then remove cash discount from the new amount: ₦45,000 x 0.95 = ₦42,750. Trade discount dey come first before cash discount.

questions.q: An invoice from a trading company in Enugu carries the term "Net 30 days". What does this term mean to the buyer?
o: The buyer gets a 30% discount if payment is made within 30 days
The goods must be delivered to the buyer within 30 days
The buyer must pay 30% of the amount immediately as deposit
Full payment must be made within 30 days, with no discount allowed
questions.e: "Net 30 days" is a payment term meaning the full invoice amount is due within 30 days of the invoice date, and no cash discount applies for early payment. It only states a deadline, not a discount or delivery condition.
questions.p: "Net 30 days" mean say the buyer must pay the full money wey dey invoice within 30 days, no discount dey for am. E just be deadline, e no be about discount or delivery.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines electronic commerce (e-commerce)?
o: The storage of business records in filing cabinets
The use of computers only to type business letters
The buying and selling of goods and services through the internet
The process of manufacturing goods using machines
questions.e: E-commerce means carrying out business transactions such as buying and selling using electronic means like the internet. Typing letters or manufacturing goods with machines are not e-commerce.
questions.p: E-commerce na when people dey buy and sell goods and services through internet. To type letter with computer or use machine to produce goods no be e-commerce.

questions.q: Which device allows a bank customer to withdraw cash electronically without entering the banking hall?
questions.e: An ATM is a self-service machine that allows customers to withdraw cash, check balance and perform other transactions without going inside the banking hall. POS is for payment at shops, not cash withdrawal from a bank directly in this way, and barcode scanners and fax machines do not dispense cash.
questions.p: ATM na machine wey customer go use withdraw money without entering bank hall. POS dey for payment for shop, barcode scanner and fax machine no fit give person cash.

questions.q: In e-commerce, when a manufacturing company in Aba sells raw materials directly to another company in Kano through an online platform, this type of transaction is best described as:
questions.e: Since the transaction is between two businesses (one company selling to another company), it is classified as Business-to-Business (B2B). It is not B2C because no individual consumer is involved, and not C2C or C2B since individuals are not the sellers.
questions.p: Since na company dey sell to another company, e be Business-to-Business (B2B). E no be B2C because no ordinary person dey buy, and e no be C2C or C2B because no individual dey sell.

questions.q: One major advantage of using computers in business record keeping, compared to manual methods, is that computers:
o: remove the need for trained staff entirely
guarantee that goods will never go out of stock
process and retrieve large volumes of data quickly and accurately
eliminate the need for business capital
questions.e: Computers can store, process and retrieve large amounts of business data faster and more accurately than manual filing systems. They do not remove the need for capital, staff, or guarantee stock levels, which depend on other business decisions.
questions.p: Computer fit process and bring out plenty business data fast and correct, pass paper work. E no mean say business no go need money, staff, or say goods no go ever finish.

questions.q: A key challenge limiting the growth of e-commerce in many parts of Nigeria is:
o: excess number of computer literate customers
poor internet connectivity and epileptic power supply
too many banks offering online services
overproduction of goods by local manufacturers
questions.e: E-commerce depends heavily on stable internet access and constant electricity; where these are poor, online transactions are slowed down or disrupted. Having many banks online or computer-literate customers would actually help, not hinder, e-commerce.
questions.p: E-commerce need good internet and steady light to work well; if network and power no good, e go hinder online business. Plenty banks online or people wey sabi computer go help, no be wahala.

questions.q: Mrs. Chidinma wants to set up an online shop where she sells fabrics directly to individual customers who order and pay for them from their homes. Which type of e-commerce model is she adopting?
questions.e: Since Mrs. Chidinma (a business owner) is selling directly to individual customers for personal use, this is Business-to-Consumer (B2C). It is not C2C because she is a business, not a fellow consumer, and not G2B or B2B since no government or company is involved as the buyer.
questions.p: Because na business owner dey sell direct to ordinary customer for personal use, na Business-to-Consumer (B2C). E no be C2C because she no be fellow consumer, and e no be G2B or B2B since no government or company dey buy.

questions.q: Why do online shopping websites use encryption software during payment transactions?
o: To increase the price of goods sold online
To reduce the number of visitors to the website
To protect customers' card and personal details from being stolen
To make the website load slower for security
questions.e: Encryption scrambles sensitive data such as card numbers and passwords so that hackers cannot easily read or steal them during online transactions. It has nothing to do with raising prices, reducing visitors, or slowing the site deliberately.
questions.p: Encryption dey scramble important information like card number and password so that hackers no go fit steal am easily when person dey pay online. E no concern price, visitors, or make site slow.
